title: Engineering ATLAS: the dynamic-range law and its retraction ledger
description:
An instrument short of dynamic range does not return a cautious answer. It reports that the quantity is bounded, which is the most reassuring wrong answer available.

This record derives the critical headroom ρ* below which a maximum-likelihood generalised-Pareto fit crosses into that failure, as the root of E[Z2] = 2 (E[Z])2 on the censored observable Z = min(Y, ρ). ρ* is not a constant: it has an interior minimum of 4.2424 at ξ = 0.3243, takes the exact algebraic values 3√2 at ξ = 1/3 and 15/2 at ξ = 2, and diverges as ξ → 0, so near-exponential tails are the expensive case for instrument design rather than the cheap one.

It also scopes the result: the failure belongs to maximum-likelihood estimation, not to instruments in general. Hill can never report a bounded tail because it is non-negative by construction, and Pickands is exactly invariant to any ceiling above the threshold because it discards precisely the data the ceiling corrupts — avoidance, not correction.

The record includes a ledger of every claim the project made and then withdrew, with the mechanism that caught each one.
